1. POSITION DESCRIPTION
JOB Title: Support Lead - NDIS
JOB TYPE: Full Time
LOCATION: Head Office and Hurlstone Park
SUPERVISOR/MANAGER: NDIS Managers
Deputy: N/A
Authorities: Work Health and Safety and NDIS Operations

2. MAIN DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES
- Coordinate Together Two’s Client Management System to ensure NDIS compliance.
- Effectively coordinate services to a high quality, ensuring service user choice, control and flexibility is maximised.
- Coordinate NDIS funded services that meet, Together Two’s service delivery requirements to ensure ongoing compliance with the NDIS Practice Standards.
- Ensure all services comply with Together Two’s policies and procedures.
- Facilitate an organisational culture that is positive, effective, and supportive for volunteers, staff, and clients.
- Support the disability support work team to work collaboratively with all program areas of Together Two.
- Create and maintain a workplace culture which attracts and retains skilled staff.
- Ensure that the workplace is harassment and discrimination free for staff, clients, and volunteers.
- Provide supervision, support, and performance monitoring to disability support staff to facilitate the achievement of individual and organisational objectives.
- Coordinate EEO and WH&S policies and practices to ensure equitable and inclusive practices
- Ensure a professional and ethical approach is practiced by all staff.
- Work effectively with the wider Together Two team to ensure that staff are accountable for their work and actions including adherence to company policy and procedures.
- Be a professional role model to all staff and volunteers, demonstrating positive leadership qualities.
- Support clients to participate in age-appropriate activities and tasks including employment, in home support and
community access.
- Support clients to access activities and outings in the community.
- Provide direct assistance to each client in accordance with their service plan and as directed
- Work in accordance with the medication administration policy, work health and safety procedures and client right's policies including privacy and confidentiality.
- Monitor the safety and well-being of the clients and report any concerns to the relevant NDIS Manager.
- Ensure completion of appropriate documentation. Relevant information on support provided is to be recorded in client notes and communication book as required.
- Lead Lifestyle Service Planning process for individual clients and monitor outcomes.
- Work with clients, family/ carers, relevant case managers and other professionals to support the client's individual goals.
- In conjunction with other members of staff assist in developing, implementing, and evaluating training and behaviour programs to attain identified individual goals.
- Ensure that all programming undertaken is appropriately maintained, documented, and reviewed.
- Assume the role of key worker for designated clients, including the preparation of a monthly report on client progress.
- Liaise extensively with other staff to ensure the overall smooth and consistent running of the service.
- Actively contribute to a team environment through open communication, participation in regular staff meetings, planning processes and policy review.
- Provide back up and support in the absence of disability support staff as necessary.
- Participate in Performance Development meetings to identify ongoing training and support opportunities.
- Notify the service if you are unable to work your rostered shifts, with as much notice as possible.
- Contribute to NDIS Reviews as directed by the relevant NDIS Manager.
- Take reasonable care for his or her own health and safety
- Take reasonable care that his/her acts or omissions do not adversely affect the health and safety

3. QUALIFICATIONS
- Diploma in Individual Support, Case Management or Community Services and/or extensive experience in leading disability support services (Essential)
- Bachelor Level Qualification in relevant area (Desirable)
- Relevant qualifications in community sector management (Desirable)

4. COMPETENCIES AND EXPERIENCE
Experience 
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in disability (NDIS) services.
- Experience of managing complex behavior support needs.
- Experience of leading teams
- Demonstrated knowledge of the NDIS and NDIS Practice Standards.

SUMMARY:
- Looking for candidates available to work:
Mon morning
Tue morning
Wed morning
Thu morning
Fri morning
- 2-3 years of relevant work experience required for this role
- Expected salary: $77,000 - $85,000 per year

result.description: SHINING PEARL PTY LTD  Shining Pearl Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Construction Estimator to join its growing team in Victoria. This role is responsible for assessing property damage, preparing accurate estimates, coordinating restoration works, and ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, safely, and to the highest quality standards.   Benefits  Salary plus Superannuation   Task & responsibilities   Conduct detailed on-site inspections to assess fire, water, mould, storm, and other property damage.  Evaluate damage in accordance with construction plans, Australian Standards, building regulations, and relevant codes of practice.  Prepare comprehensive cost estimates, quotations, scopes of work, and restoration reports for residential and commercial projects.  Calculate labour, material, plant, equipment, subcontractor, and overhead costs to develop accurate project budgets.  Estimate project durations, resource requirements, and completion schedules.  Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications, and insurance documentation to determine project requirements.  Coordinate restoration projects from commencement through to completion, ensuring works are delivered within approved budgets and timeframes.  Monitor project progress and conduct site inspections to verify quality, compliance, and contract requirements.  Liaise with clients, insurance representatives, project coordinators, contractors, suppliers, and trades throughout project delivery.  Source materials and services, obtain supplier quotations, and negotiate competitive pricing and delivery schedules.  Prepare tender submissions, variation estimates, progress claims, and supporting documentation where required.    Identify project risks, recommend practical restoration solutions, and implement cost-effective strategies without compromising quality.  Maintain accurate project records, cost reports, estimating databases, and documentation using estimating software and Microsoft Office applications.  Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety legislation, environmental requirements, and company policies.  Deliver exceptional customer service by responding promptly and professionally to client enquiries and project-related concerns.  Travel to various project sites across Victoria and respond to emergency restoration call-outs as required. At least 1-2 years of experience as a Construction Estimator or in a similar role.  Driver's license  Strong understanding of residential and commercial construction methods, building materials, and restoration practices.  Experience estimating insurance repair, restoration, or construction projects is highly regarded.  Strong communication, negotiation, organisational, and stakeholder management skills.  Ability to prioritise multiple projects and work autonomously in a fast-paced environment. About the Role
Perth Plate and REO are seeking a Recruitment Consultant to join our team.
This role is responsible for managing end-to-end recruitment activities, supporting the ongoing workforce requirements of Perth Plate and REO, as well as providing recruitment support to related entities within the wider business structure where required.
Due to ongoing operational requirements and continued recruitment demand, this position will play an important role in attracting, assessing and selecting suitable candidates to support our workforce needs.
Key Responsibilities
•	Receive and review recruitment requirements from managers, including position details, duties, skills requirements, experience requirements, employment conditions and workforce needs. 
•	Prepare, develop and advertise job vacancies through recruitment platforms including SEEK and other relevant channels. 
•	Source suitable candidates through job advertisements, recruitment databases, referrals and other recruitment methods. 
•	Review applications, screen candidates and assess suitability against position requirements. 
•	Conduct interviews and candidate assessments to identify suitable applicants. 
•	Coordinate the recruitment process from vacancy identification through to candidate selection and commencement. 
•	Provide recruitment recommendations and updates to managers regarding candidate suitability and recruitment progress. 
•	Communicate with candidates regarding available positions, role requirements and employment conditions. 
•	Maintain accurate candidate records, recruitment documentation and recruitment reporting. 
•	Coordinate reference checks, pre-employment checks and onboarding activities. 
•	Maintain recruitment activity records and monitor vacancy progress. 
•	Manage recruitment activities for Perth Plate and REO, while providing recruitment support to related businesses where required.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
•	A qualification in Human Resources, Business, Recruitment or a related field (preferred). 
•	Minimum 3 years’ experience in recruitment, talent acquisition or a similar role. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing end-to-end recruitment processes. 
•	Strong experience in candidate sourcing, screening, interviewing and selection. 
•	Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. 
•	Ability to manage multiple vacancies and competing priorities. 
•	Strong organisational skills and attention to detail. 
•	Ability to build effective relationships with managers, candidates and employees.
What We Offer
•	Full-time opportunity with a salary of $80000.00 plus superannuation.
•	Ongoing training and skill development
•	Supportive, friendly and experienced team
•	Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), providing confidential counselling and wellbeing support for employees and their immediate family members.
